ports.note: Three inputs rather than the pack's two: a table has no geometry (fw:DataTable is disjoint from fw:PointDataset), so the published sites must arrive as a point layer rather than inside the projections table. The output is a table of distances, so the join itself can be displayed and checked.

ontology.note: Maps to the sea-level pack's vocabulary, vendored into ontology/packs/sea-level.ttl at the digest widgets/packs.json pins. This widget mints no host term: the pack's namespace stays authoritative for the meaning. See docs/experiments/58-sea-level-widgets.md. The receipt is constrained by slr:ProjectionValueShape, slr:SiteAssignmentShape and slr:ThresholdComparisonShape in ontology/shapes/pack-sea-level.ttl, verified in tests; this registry version records application validation only, so the shapes are not referenced in a field.

changes.description: Retired into Measure distance and Relate (experiment 197). Read operation by operation, it held none about sea level: the nearest site and its distance is Measure distance, through the same shared search; keeping only sites the projections file holds is Measure distance's candidate condition or Relate's unmatched rows; the projection at the site is Relate after Select rows. A table port now accepts a distances result, read as a table keyed by point_id, nearest_id and the nearest candidate's own attributes. Retired outright: no outside user.

evidence.note: Unit checks cover nearest assignment, retained distance, unlocated points and refusal of a site layer whose identifiers are absent from the extract. Assignment is not a claim that the projection applies at the point; the distance is recorded so a reader can judge that.
